claims.statement: The test suite is a single xunit project at tests/Sebastian.Tests targeting net10.0 with a ProjectReference to Sebastian.csproj and a global `<Using Include="Xunit" />`; because the repository has no solution file, `dotnet test tests/Sebastian.Tests/Sebastian.Tests.csproj` and `dotnet build Sebastian.csproj` are the entry points, and no test file needs a `using Xunit;`.

The pairing of `<InternalsVisibleTo Include="Sebastian.Tests" />` with `<DefaultItemExcludes>…;tests/**</DefaultItemExcludes>` in the product project file is what lets every service stay `internal sealed` while tests construct those types directly, and it also guarantees the web project never compiles the test tree, so making a member `public` for test visibility is unnecessary.

The test project is a deliberately less strict compilation than the product: it does not set TreatWarningsAsErrors, AnalysisLevel=latest-all, PublishAot, or InvariantGlobalization, so a diagnostic or AOT-unsafe construct in test code does not fail the build and test code cannot be used as AOT evidence.

`TestHostEnvironment` exists solely because `Git`'s constructor reads nothing from `IHostEnvironment` except `ContentRootPath`; the fake supplies that path plus a `NullFileProvider`, which is honest because `Git` never reads files through the content-root file provider. This is what allows `Git` to be aimed at a temporary clone.

Configuration-dependent services are tested with in-memory objects through `Options.Create(config)` rather than the binder: `ProviderResolverTests` builds a `SebastianConfig` with `GitHub = null!` because the resolver reads only `Agent`, whereas the generated-validator test must populate a full `GitHubConfig` first, since `[ValidateObjectMembers]` would otherwise report the missing section instead of the blank API key under test.

`ImplementSpec.PrepareWorkspaceAsync` is `internal` rather than private purely as a test seam, so `ImplementSpecTests` can exercise the whole workspace policy (identity check, fetch, mirror guards, fast-forward, worktree reuse or creation) with no model provider, chat client, or agent session — meaning the git half of the job is tested while `RunAsync`'s agent half is not.

`AgentRole.CreateOptions()` is `internal` as a test seam: `AgentRoleTests` asserts a `FakeRole`'s override reaches the option graph and that `ImplementationAgent` yields a file store with write tools enabled, one AI context provider, and exactly one tool — none of which requires an `IChatClient` or a network call.

`TestRepository` is a real-git, offline fixture: it initializes a bare origin at `<temp>/owner/repo.git`, clones it through a `file://` URL, commits and pushes a seeded `README.md`, and exposes `CreateGit()` returning `new Git(new TestHostEnvironment(work), NullLogger<Git>.Instance)`; consequently the four `ImplementSpecTests` cases require a `git` binary on PATH and a writable temp filesystem but no network or credentials.

The fixture's `<root>/owner/repo.git` layout is load-bearing, not cosmetic: `RepositoryIdentity.Parse` takes the last two segments of the remote URL, so the temp origin parses to `owner`/`repo`, which is what makes `RejectsForeignRepository` throw for `new ImplementSpec("other", "repo", …)` instead of failing for an unrelated reason.

Every `ImplementSpecTests` case calls `await git.StartAsync(...)` before preparing a workspace because `Git.Repository` is populated only by `EnsureRepositoryAsync`, and `PrepareWorkspaceAsync` treats a null `Repository` as "hosted service not started" and throws.

`ImplementSpecTests` pins exactly four workspace behaviors — an existing worktree is reused and an uncommitted marker file survives, a worktree removed with `git worktree remove --force` is recreated at the same path, a dirty local `main` makes preparation throw, and a mismatched owner makes preparation throw — which exercises two of the three `FindMirrorProblemAsync` reasons; the "commits ahead of origin/main" and "not on main" branches have no test.

`JobQueueTests` builds the queue directly over an empty `ServiceCollection().BuildServiceProvider()` and a `NullLogger`, with a local `TestJob` that signals its completion `TaskCompletionSource` in a `finally`; the three tests pin the effective concurrency cap of ten (twelve gated jobs, exactly ten started before release), that a throwing job neither escapes the handler nor stops the loop, and that a key is refused while its job runs and accepted again after completion.

The `JobQueue` shutdown and cancellation paths have no test: nothing asserts `TryAdd` returns false after `StopAsync`, that buffered jobs are abandoned rather than run, or that either `OperationCanceledException` filter suppresses a cancelled job without logging it as a failure.

`RepositoryIdentityTests` pins remote parsing as two theories: the four supported shapes (`https://…` with and without `.git`, scp-like `git@…:owner/repo.git`, `ssh://…`) all yield `owner`/`repo`, and the empty string, a non-remote string, and an owner-only URL all return null.

`SpecTemplateValidatorTests` duplicates the seven required section names as its own array rather than reading the production list, so editing `SpecTemplateValidator.RequiredSections` breaks a test; the file also pins that lowercase headings, CRLF line endings, `###` subheadings and unknown sections are tolerated, that `Further Notes` is optional, and that a null body reports all seven. It therefore pins the validator against itself, not against `skills/to-spec/SKILL.md`, which nothing reads.

`ProviderResolverTests` pins the three fail-fast conditions of `ProviderResolver` by message text (unconfigured selected provider, duplicate provider names, empty provider list), asserts `CreateChatClient()` returns non-null without any network access, and proves that a whitespace-only `ApiKey` is rejected by the generated `ValidateSebastianConfig` rather than by the resolver's constructor.

Nothing in the suite exercises intake or GitHub writes: no test references `GitHubWebhookProcessor`, `GitHubService`, `PostCommentAsync`, or `CloseIssueAsync`, and there is no `WebApplicationFactory`, so the action list, label checks, spec-before-approval ordering, comment text, `not_planned` close, enqueue path, PEM import, and token adapter all rest on review alone. Making the processor testable requires first introducing a seam, because it takes concrete `GitHubService`, `Git` and `JobQueue` instances and constructs `ImplementSpec` inline.

No test starts an agent: `RunAsync`'s provider resolution, session creation, model turn, `git status` read, and completion log are unexercised, and no test creates a `HarnessAgent`. The available but unused seam is `AgentRole.CreateAgent(IChatClient)`, which would accept a fake client; `AgentRoleTests` instead carries the MAAI001/MEAI001 pragmas because it touches the harness option types directly and disposes a constructed `ImplementationAgent` with `await using`.

`Git.SyncMainAsync` has no test of its own: the `ImplementSpecTests` calls to `StartAsync` incidentally cover only the happy startup path against a file remote, so the ref filter, the behind-count short-circuit, the swallow-on-failure behavior, and the ten-second bound are unverified.

`TestRepository` exposes more surface than the suite uses: `LocalHead`, `RemoteHead`, `RemoteTrackingHead`, `CloneAgain`, `CommitFile`, and `HeadAt` are referenced by no test (only the static `RunGit` is used from outside the fixture), so the scaffolding a mirror-sync test would need already exists but is currently dead weight.

There is no CI pipeline for the test suite. The repository's only workflow, `.github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml`, installs OpenWiki, runs `openwiki code --update`, deletes transient run state, and opens a documentation pull request; it never builds, tests, or publishes Sebastian, so a failed run signals a documentation failure rather than a code failure.

`EnvironmentPlaceholdersTests` is the only test that drives the product's configuration-placeholder layer: it calls the public `ExpandEnvironmentPlaceholders` extension on a `ConfigurationManager` fed by `AddInMemoryCollection` and pins that a whole-value `{env:NAME}` is replaced from the process environment while a literal value is untouched, and that an unset variable makes expansion throw an `InvalidOperationException` whose message names both the environment variable and the configuration key.

Because `EnvironmentPlaceholdersTests` mutates process-global environment variables, it isolates itself with a freshly generated `SEBASTIAN_TEST_<guid>` variable name per case and clears it in a `finally`, which keeps the otherwise-parallel suite free of cross-test interference; the suite has no other shared mutable state.

`FindMissingSections` treats a null body as empty and varies only the ordering of the seven production section names, so `NullBody_ReportsAllRequiredSections` asserts the result equals the test's own `RequiredSections` array and additionally pins that the reported order matches `SpecTemplateValidator.RequiredSections`.

`EnvironmentPlaceholders` has partially covered edges: inline interpolation is unsupported by design (the `shortcut` comment scopes it to whole-value placeholders) and an empty `{env:}` name is treated as missing, but neither an empty name nor whitespace-only variable values has a test — only the unset-variable path is pinned.

`Program.cs` composition has no integration coverage and is therefore unverified by the suite: the `ExpandEnvironmentPlaceholders()` call at startup, the binding-plus-generated-validator registration, and the factory-style registrations that make `Git` and `JobQueue` the same instance as their hosted-service descriptors would all be removable without a failing test.

`TestRepository` fixes a deterministic commit identity by setting `user.name`/`user.email` locally in the clone (and in every `CloneAgain()` result) rather than relying on global git configuration, which is what makes the fixture reproducible on a clean machine or CI runner.
